To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Appearance features are highly unstable under change of aspect and 2) It is possible to construct features that are stable under change of viewpoint, without requiring any examples of the activity from the new aspect.

appearance features are highly discriminative for a given aspect of the scene, but that aspect can change drastically from frame to frame, and that the appearance features are not stable enough to discriminate across aspect.

appearance is a good feature for activity recognition, but that appearance is not invariant to aspect change, and that one can use unlabeled data to build a model of how appearance varies with aspect.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of how to build appearance models of activities that are robust to change in aspect, and we present a solution that is based on a new class of discriminative features that can be learned from unlabeled data.
how we might learn to recognize activities from a view different from that in which we learn to recognize them.
the problem of recognizing activities from the wrong view point.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a new approach that is capable of recognizing activities across views.
our method can recognize activities that are not visible from the viewpoint where they were learned.
we have shown that it is possible to learn a model of activity in the wrong viewpoint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to build features that can be used to recognize activities from a different viewpoint, even though no examples are available in that view.
we show it is possible to recognize activities from the wrong view point.
we are able to learn a model of activity from a single view, and then use it to recognize the activity in other views.
The main takeaway from our work is that
appearance is not a reliable feature for recognition of human activity.
we can use the wrong view to spot an activity, and we can do so with only unlabeled examples.
we can build features that are robust to aspect change, without the need for multiple views.
